correctness.rationale: The source defines L_b as the upward principal scattered-subsequence ideal for 00 1^b and root via concatenation w w, b any integer >=1, binary alphabet, complete DFAs. Direct embedding analysis gives: zero zeros => reject; one zero in 1^p01^t => accept iff t>=b; >=2 zeros with first two in 1^p01^h0u => accept iff p+h+2|u|_1 >= b. The leading p ones in the second copy are correctly included. For any suffix, this yields exactly quotient types P_p (0<=p<=b), Q_(alpha,beta) (1<=alpha<=b, 0<=beta<=alpha), R_j (1<=j<=ceil b/2), and absorbing A, with the sole identification Q_(1,1)=R_1. Prefix witnesses 1^p, 1^(alpha-beta)01^(b-alpha), 00 followed by ones, and 01^b establish reachability. The exact distinguishing suffixes in RESULT.md separate A, all P, all Q by alpha or beta, all R by j, and Q/R (including alpha=beta=j>=2 via 01^ceil(j/2)), proving minimality by Myhill–Nerode, not by finite extrapolation. Their count is (b+1)+(b(b+3)/2-1)+ceil(b/2)+1=ceil(b^2/2)+3b+1, including b=1. The sequential-matching complete DFA of the original pattern 00 1^b has b+3 distinct stages. The actual seven Git blob identities recombine to the assigned tree SHA. Fresh separate code tested 40,940 direct doubled-word instances against the two-zero criterion for b<=20, independently minimized the true transformation-monoid root automaton for b<=10, and verified 37,667 Myhill–Nerode distinguishing-pair witnesses for b<=14. The finite tests are corroboration of the explicit universal proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original as the all-b fixed-alphabet complete-DFA quotient count for the square root of the binary principal superword ideal generated by 00 1^b. Guyot gives an exponential lower bound for varying-alphabet distinct-letter upward generators and an exact quadratic count for a DIFFERENT downward-closed cyclic family. Onishchenko gives the n^3 NFA worst-case for arbitrary regular languages with growing alphabet, without this concrete deterministic binary family. Two nearby published exact state-complexity results count an F2 parity automaton root or words with exactly k scattered 01 occurrences, neither of which implies the present quotient count. An unindexed equivalent special-family enumeration could remain; unsuccessful search is not priority proof.
residual_risks: Older or unindexed state-complexity literature may hide equivalent binary principal-ideal or word-root state enumeration; bounded primary and semantic searches do not establish historical priority.

value.rationale: The state complexity of a fixed binary principal superword ideal under the standard language-square-root operator is a natural structural invariant in finite-state descriptional complexity. Exact all-parameter quadratic growth from b+3 to ceil(b^2/2)+3b+1, with a canonical four-type quotient DFA and the nontrivial Q_(1,1)=R_1 merger, is a motivated sharp fixed-alphabet complexity separation. It is not a textbook parameter substitution from Guyot’s growing-alphabet lower bounds nor a recomputation of a known table. It offers an explicit useful benchmark family and a complete threshold-classification proof. Does not claim worst-case optimality across all upward-closed languages, all alphabets, higher roots or NFAs.
residual_risks: The example is a specialized family rather than a general bound; its relevance is to fixed-alphabet parametric structure and benchmark construction.
